response.text:
Action items (from the raw notes)
1. Deploy failures on Friday afternoons
   - Triage: collect deploy logs/metrics for Friday deploys and compare with other days. Owner: SRE/Dev lead. Due: this week.
   - Reproduce & root-cause: schedule time to reproduce failure pattern and identify the cause. Owner: on-call or dev who owns deployment pipeline.
   - Mitigation: if cause not immediately fixable, move or block Friday-afternoon deploys and add automated rollback on failure. Owner: Release manager.
   - Monitoring/runbook: add an alert and a runbook for Friday deploy failures. Owner: SRE.

2. Nobody owns the staging DB
   - Assign an owner and backup/maintenance responsibilities for the staging DB. Owner: engineering manager (assign to a person).
   - Define access, change process, and SLAs for staging. Owner: DB/admin or assigned owner.
   - Add a runbook for common staging DB tasks (reset, seed, restore). Owner: assigned owner.
   - Schedule a short review to confirm owner handoff and document responsibilities. Owner: manager.

3. Marcus’ attendance/early departures
   - Manager/private check-in: manager to reach out privately to Marcus to ask if he’s okay and whether any accommodations or adjustments are needed. Owner: Marcus’ manager. Due: ASAP.
   - Temporary coverage plan: identify who will cover responsibilities if Marcus is unavailable and update team calendar/standup coverage. Owner: team lead.
   - Track attendance pattern (dates/times) so there’s factual documentation if needed. Owner: team lead/manager.

4. QA wants a pre-merge checklist
   - Create a pre-merge checklist (required items: passing CI, unit/integration tests, QA sign-off, security scan, migration review, documented rollback plan). Owner: QA lead + tech lead. Due: next sprint.
   - Integrate checklist into PR template and CI gate so merges cannot proceed until checklist items are confirmed. Owner: repo admin / Dev lead.
   - Communicate checklist and enforcement plan to the team. Owner: QA lead.

If you want, I can format these into tasks for your tracker (with suggested owners and deadlines).

About Marcus: I can’t and shouldn’t infer private reasons (health, family, etc.) from attendance notes. Speculating about personal matters is inappropriate and unreliable.

Recommended next steps instead
- Do a private, supportive check-in (manager). Example script: “I’ve noticed you missed a couple of standups and left early a few times — I wanted to check in to see if everything’s OK or if there’s anything you need from us.” Keep it open-ended, non-judgmental.
- Offer options: flexible hours, brief time off, EAP/HR support, or temporary workload adjustments.
- If Marcus prefers privacy, respect that while documenting impacts and arranging coverage.
- Escalate to HR if there are policy, performance, or safety concerns, or if Marcus requests formal support.

If you’d like, I can draft a short private message/check-in you can send to Marcus.
